normative_terms.byte_order: little-endian for every integer and IEEE-754 bit pattern
normative_terms.hash: SHA-256 with the exact bytes and domain tags declared below; hexadecimal appears only in JSON receipts
normative_terms.ascii: Every tag and tensor name is exact 7-bit ASCII with no implicit terminator except the common-header magic's declared NUL
normative_terms.integer_width: uint8, uint16, uint32, and uint64 have exactly 1, 2, 4, and 8 bytes
normative_terms.float_width: float observations are exact finite IEEE-754 binary32 bits bit-cast to uint32; NaN or infinity aborts
normative_terms.write_rule: Every stream uses complete retry-on-EINTR writes, rejects short writes and arithmetic overflow, fsyncs before close, and publishes no footer after any observation failure
normative_terms.comparison_rule: Digests are comparable only when population, coordinate, count, format, source, and layout bindings match; arm and direction comparisons are those explicitly authorized below

fields_in_order: offset 0: 7 ASCII bytes GMCOBS2 followed by one NUL byte
offset 32: 32 raw bytes complete v6 candidate source-tree SHA-256
offset 64: 32 raw bytes this exact ABI artifact SHA-256
offset 96: 32 raw bytes exact v6 component-layout artifact SHA-256
offset 128: 32 raw bytes exact raw-population SHA-256
offset 160: 32 raw bytes exact reversible modeled-stream SHA-256
common_header.open_rule: Create each stream with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC beneath a pre-opened absolute result-directory descriptor. Reject symlinks, existing paths, non-regular files, path escape, open/write/seek/fsync/close failure, and geometry overflow.
common_header.identity_rule: Both streams for one run have byte-identical common fields except stream_kind. Encoder and decoder differ only in direction and direction-specific observations.

fields_in_order: 32 raw bytes SHA-256 over every byte after the 192-byte header and before this footer
common_footer.clean_eof_rule: Write the footer only after complete successful observation, fsync it, close successfully, and require immediate EOF. Missing, duplicate, partial, trailing, count-inconsistent, body-size-inconsistent, or digest-inconsistent footers reject the stream.

probability.record_preimage: For every coded bit in order, append the exact final uint16 probability immediately before the arithmetic split.
probability.count_rule: Exactly modeled_events*8 records for the frozen byte population.
probability.checkpoint_rule: Clone-finalize the live SHA-256 context without reset at each sparse checkpoint.

component_boundary.record_preimage: For every completed coded-bit Predictor::Perceive in order, append uint64 zero-based coded-bit ordinal, uint32 exact bits of ByteMixer::Predict()[0] assigned to byte_mixer_output, and uint32 bit-cast bits of ByteModel::ex.
component_boundary.count_rule: Exactly one boundary record after every coded bit and exactly modeled_events*8 records total.
component_boundary.checkpoint_rule: Clone-finalize the live SHA-256 context without reset at each sparse checkpoint.
component_boundary.source_rule: The observer hook runs immediately after byte_mixer_output and lstmex are assigned and before Predictor::Perceive returns. It must not call Predict again or mutate component/environment state.

payload_prefix.record_preimage: Append each payload byte in payload-file order exactly once.
payload_prefix.encoder_rule: Hash logically emitted bytes, including bytes still in the coder's output buffer, and report that logical prefix length.
payload_prefix.decoder_rule: Hash physically consumed payload bytes and report that consumed prefix length.
payload_prefix.comparison_rule: Intermediate values compare only across arms or repeats in the same direction at the same coordinate. Final payload files and their ordinary file SHA-256 must match encoder/decode within arm.

checkpoint.record_framing: tag[4], uint32 record_bytes=204, uint8 checkpoint_kind, uint8 hook_phase, uint16 reserved=0, uint32 range_low, uint32 range_high, uint32 range_code, uint32 coder_aux, uint64 modeled_events, uint64 coded_bits, uint64 probability_records, uint64 component_records, uint64 midpoint_update_records, uint64 payload_prefix_bytes, probability_sha256[32], component_boundary_sha256[32], payload_prefix_sha256[32], component_state_root_sha256[32]

hook_phases.0: After model construction, retained pretraining, observer initialization, and the start component-state rebuild; immediately before the first modeled BeginTraceByte.
hook_phases.1: Immediately after EndTraceByte at modeled-event coordinate 33, after the first closure's adapted boundary output and update record are available.
hook_phases.2: Immediately after EndTraceByte at modeled-event coordinate 128.
hook_phases.3: Immediately after EndTraceByte at floor(population modeled_events/2).
hook_phases.4: Immediately after the final EndTraceByte and before Encoder::Flush or decoder finalization.
hook_phases.5: Immediately after Encoder::Flush or successful decoder finalization; component state and probability/component digests must equal terminal_pre_flush while payload evidence may advance.

checkpoint.coordinate_rule: Every allowed population is at least 250,000 modeled events, so the six rows are ordered start=0, first_closure=33, first_native_horizon=128, population_midpoint=floor(N/2), terminal_pre_flush=N, finalization=N. Exactly one row of every kind exists; the two terminal-coordinate rows remain distinct.
checkpoint.count_rule: Exactly six checkpoint records per stream.
checkpoint.coder_fields: Encoder sets range_code=0 and records exact low/high/coder_aux; decoder records low/high/code/coder_aux. No encoder/decoder coder-state equality is inferred.
checkpoint.state_rule: Every row contains a fresh full component root over all 141 typed tensors and partition codes 1,2,3,4,6,7 under the exact v6 layout.

update.record_framing: tag[4], uint32 record_bytes=256, uint64 update_ordinal, uint64 segment_start_modeled_events, uint64 closure_modeled_events, uint64 boundary_record_count, uint64 probability_record_count, uint32 native_start_phase, uint32 closure_phase, uint8 arm, uint8 committed, uint8 detached, uint8 target_rotation, uint8 k_dynamic_equal, three reserved zero bytes, source_symbols_sha256[32], unrotated_targets_sha256[32], pre_restore_dynamic_sha256[32], post_replay_dynamic_sha256[32], cumulative_probability_sha256[32], cumulative_component_boundary_sha256[32]
update.coordinate_formula: For zero-based update ordinal u: segment_start_modeled_events=64*u, closure_modeled_events=33+64*u, native_start_phase=(64*u)%128, closure_phase=native_start_phase+32, and both rolling record counts equal 8*closure_modeled_events.
update.arm_rule: P emits no rows. K emits the formula count with arm=1, committed=0, detached=1, target_rotation=0, k_dynamic_equal=1. F emits the formula count with arm=2, committed=1, detached=0, target_rotation=0, k_dynamic_equal=0. S emits the formula count with arm=3, committed=1, detached=0, target_rotation=16, k_dynamic_equal=0.
update.timing: Retain the four local digests while their preimages exist, clear scratch, finish the component boundary observation for the closure event, then append the row before its matching first_closure checkpoint or the next modeled event. No full gradient, parameter, optimizer, or cleared-scratch reread is required.
update.source_symbols_digest: SHA-256 over 8 ASCII bytes GMCSYMB2 followed by the 32 source-order midpoint_symbols_ values as uint32LE.
update.unrotated_targets_digest: SHA-256 over 8 ASCII bytes GMCTARG2 followed by the 32 source-order midpoint_targets_ values as uint32LE before the S association rotation.
update.pre_restore_dynamic_digest: SHA-256 over 8 ASCII bytes GMCPRED2, uint32LE hidden_count=272, the 272 closure-hidden f32 bit patterns, uint32LE layer_count=1, uint32LE cell_count=256, then the 256 layer-0 closure-cell f32 bit patterns.
update.post_replay_dynamic_digest: SHA-256 over 8 ASCII bytes GMCPOST2, uint32LE hidden_count=272, the 272 live post-replay hidden f32 bit patterns, uint32LE layer_count=1, uint32LE cell_count=256, then the 256 live post-replay layer-0 cell f32 bit patterns.
update.k_identity_rule: K performs bytewise comparison of the same canonical dynamic preimages, requires both digests equal, sets k_dynamic_equal=1, and aborts before publication on any mismatch.

file_geometry.update_file_formula: 248 + 256*U bytes, where U is the update count
file_geometry.interpretation: These are exact observer stream and sparse-read geometries, not codec package bytes, compression savings, or runtime measurements.

chronological_third_shadow_coders.role: Exact diagnostic control for the preregistered requirement that aligned F beat shifted S in every original-coordinate third; these payloads are not the native archive and receive no score credit.
chronological_third_shadow_coders.coordinate_rule: For raw population size N and zero-based original raw-byte coordinate r, third 0 is 0 <= r < floor(N/3), third 1 is floor(N/3) <= r < floor(2*N/3), and third 2 is floor(2*N/3) <= r < N. The reversible frontend must expose the bound original coordinate for each coded modeled byte; a non-bijective, missing, duplicated, or reordered association rejects this diagnostic.
chronological_third_shadow_coders.coder_rule: Instantiate one fresh copy of the exact native integer range coder at the first modeled byte associated with each third. Feed it the identical final uint16 probabilities and actual decoded bits used by the native coder for exactly those associated bytes, in modeled coding order, then perform the same deterministic flush at that third's end.
chronological_third_shadow_coders.artifacts: Each arm/direction emits three raw shadow payload files plus path, bytes, ordinary file SHA-256, input coded-bit count, first/last raw coordinates, return code, and clean-flush boolean. Encoder and decoder artifacts must be byte-identical within an arm; repeats must be byte-identical.
chronological_third_shadow_coders.control_rule: At 10MB, for each third independently, F shadow payload bytes must be strictly smaller than both P and S. The global 40,793-byte threshold is still measured only on the native complete arithmetic archive.
chronological_third_shadow_coders.isolation_rule: Shadow coders never feed probabilities, state, bytes, or flush effects back into the native coder, component, environment, frontend, inverse, or package. Observer-off neutrality must prove their complete absence from the release path.

comparison_contract.within_arm_direction: Encoder/decode probability and component digests/counts must match at corresponding semantic coordinates; final payload file, modeled inverse, and raw inverse must match the bound population.
comparison_contract.p_k: P-A and K-A must match every complete probability and component digest, payload/archive/inverse artifact, corresponding sparse component root, and final package member. Every K update row must pass its inline dynamic identity rule.
comparison_contract.f_repeat: F-A and F-B must match source, binary, checkpoint/update streams after normalizing replicate header byte, every digest/count, payload/archive/inverse, package, and resource-policy decision.
comparison_contract.s_repeat: S-A and S-B must satisfy the same complete repeat surface.
comparison_contract.aligned_shifted: Before their first update, F and S must match. At each corresponding update, source-symbol and unrotated-target digests match; source audit proves target_rotation is the sole treatment/control association difference. No state equality is expected after the first update. At 10MB, the three fresh-start third shadow payloads must each place F strictly below P and S.
comparison_contract.failure_rule: The first missing, malformed, non-finite, misordered, count-inconsistent, digest-inconsistent, P/K-different, encoder/decode-different, repeat-different, inverse-failing, or source-closure-failing fact is an implementation/observability failure and forbids scientific interpretation.

thresholds.250000: F archive is strictly smaller than P and S after every exactness predicate passes.
thresholds.1000000: F saves at least 4,080 arithmetic archive bytes over P and strictly beats S.

scientific_contract.authority: The midpoint oracle remains zero objective credit even on a positive causal result; it authorizes only the separately identified persistence-attribution successor.

receipt_contract.direction_rule: Every logical run has independently emitted and independently parsed encode and decode streams.
receipt_contract.parser_independence: The parser/verifier must not import, compile, link, or invoke observer-emitter code. It independently rederives binary framing, body/file hashes, record geometry, count and coordinate formulas, flag semantics, and cross-run comparisons. Online probability, boundary, and component-state digests are observed values whose preimage-hook correctness is established separately by source audit, mutation controls, and observer neutrality; the parser must not pretend to reconstruct absent per-bit or tensor preimages.
receipt_contract.registry_policy: Validate schemas directly while qm8 is live. Canonical research_contracts.py registry integration is deferred until the active source-bound dispatcher terminalizes because changing its bound hash would invalidate live authority.
receipt_contract.failure_rule: Missing evidence yields an incomplete or invalid receipt, never an inferred false or positive scientific result.
